keys.explanation: DCIM ties inventory, power capacity, and change workflows to facilities data—not just environment sensing.

30134-6 is ERF (Energy Reuse Factor). ERE is not that part. The series has more than three letters; this course names the distinction and stops. No single PUE target as law. Sustainability-track depth is not this leftover.
Wrong cleaning methods can create the contamination problem they aim to solve.
Guides recommend practice; binding force comes from adoption into law, contract, or policy.
Offline/standby leaves the load on utility until a failure forces transfer—cheap but not preferred for critical core IT.
Surveys are snapshots; records enable comparison after plant or layout changes.
Single-mode supports long reach and high capacity backbone roles; multimode is common for shorter structured runs depending on design.
Supporting facilities (yard, staging, ops spaces, utility intake) are part of operability, not cosmetics.
Early detection buys time—detection is not suppression.
Monitor the chains and the monitors—blind spots include dead sensors and capacity blindness.
Layered controls (perimeter → envelope → zones → cabinets → process) assume single-layer failure.
Actionable alerts beat naked point names during incidents.

Logos are not laterals. A shared duct bank or manhole collapses both providers to one backhoe cut. That is the building oral. It is not the east-west fabric: a single-path IB/RoCE mesh remains one training job even if the laterals were actually diverse. Do not invent a reach metre.
Accidental EPO is a major outage cause; over-locking can also block emergency response.
Unverified emergency lighting is a latent life-safety failure.
Exit signs mark the means of egress; they are life-safety devices.
Cleaning is controlled work near energized systems—methods and chemistry matter.
Dual control reduces single-person error and insider risk on high-consequence actions.
Cold plates remove heat at the component rather than only via room air.
Containment integrity matters—open doors, missing panels, and cable gaps re-create recirculation paths.

ISO 19011:2018 §5.2 requires audit objectives and criteria to be defined before the audit begins. TIA-942-B and TIA-942-C have different requirement sets; an unpinned criterion leaves ambiguity about which requirements the auditor is checking. Selecting or switching editions mid-audit — or after fieldwork — compromises objectivity. The audit plan must state 'TIA-942-B Rated-3' or equivalent before the first site visit.
Protection systems only work if maintained and not casually bypassed.
Liquid-ready is a cabinet SKU, not a denser air box. 800 mm, RDHx door, drip, CDU landing, and 40–100 kW structure are the frame questions. Liquid families live in Module 09. 19″ rails stay.
International standards are tools for alignment; adoption remains a national/project decision.

Analyze the frame, not the coolant name. A 600 mm air BOM cannot dress hoses, land an RDHx door, or carry 40–100 kW. CDU landing is reserved now. Blanking stays for air-cooled network. Immersion is not a 19″ frame.
Factory trunks reduce field termination variability—still require correct design, pathways, and acceptance tests.

The November 2024 UFGS §2.1 type axis is stringer versus stringerless; a panel finish, a site rating label, and an unsupported product-class number answer different questions. The paywalled product-class boundary is deliberately not crossed.
Rolling and concentrated load ratings govern cart and equipment moves on access floors.
Managed/hosted models shift operational responsibility to a provider under contractual SLAs, with shared-responsibility nuances.
Li-ion offers density and lifecycle trade-offs, not magic immunity from engineering.

NFPA 70 (2026) §§700.12 and 700.17 tie emergency lighting to an Article 700 source and an emergency-lighting branch-circuit path when normal lighting fails. IT continuity alone does not prove that life-safety path; an UPS belongs in the answer only after the Article 700 design is verified.
Recirculation is hot air returning to intakes instead of the cooling return path.

An alarm requires operator action. Status is not an alarm. Absence of alarm is not evidence of health (2003 silent alarm-processor failure). Point-count procurement fights alarm quality. No invented outage percent.
Redundancy enables maintenance; it does not survive working the last path. Call the window N-0. Do not steal Module 06’s path grammar — this is the mission concept only.
Keep health exposure language separate from IEC 61000-class equipment immunity.
Signage supports life safety: evacuate-on-alarm messaging, agent type, and control locations.
UPS ride-through → genset start → transfer is the textbook sequence.
Basin inventory is a real-time constraint on evaporative rejection.
As water evaporates, minerals concentrate; blowdown limits scale and corrosion risk when paired with treatment.
Facility outcomes require cross-functional ownership among IT, facilities, security, and vendors.
